text: Skills use git worktree commands instead of the harness built-in worktree feature (U1).

When an epic starts it creates its own integration worktree named <epic>; task branches are named <epic>-<task>, start from and merge back into the epic integration worktree, and every agent working on a task shares that task's worktree (U2).
Once the epic is delivered and fully tested, its worktree merges back to main, then all epic and task worktrees are cleaned (U3).
Every doc and the off-Claude plan-execute fallback describe the same lifecycle; template only, the personal plugin is out of scope (D-g).

Gate answer Q1 (user, 2026-10-21: yes): inside an epic run plan-execute lands each clean, verified task on the epic integration branch (rebase onto <epic>, fast-forward in the integration tree, task verify there); dependents merge the updated <epic>; verifier and reviewer diff against <epic>; escalated tasks land only after a ruling.

Gate answer Q2 (user, 2026-10-21: yes): meta-mode epic close rebases <epic> onto main and fast-forwards main in the main checkout after the pass verdict and the full suite on the integration tree, runs the full suite on main, then move done removes every task and integration tree and branch; component mode keeps the MR path and cleans up after the MRs merge.

Interrogate verdict A: after the close rebases <epic> onto main, every merged check (continue gate, move done gate, Sweep) falls back to patch equivalence when ancestry fails; anything not equivalent is left with the reason; move done then removes every tree and branch.

Interrogate verdict B: merge.py runs the task --verify in the rebased task tree before fast-forwarding <epic>, fast-forwards only on green, re-rebases and re-verifies if <epic> moved; a failed verify never advances <epic>.

Interrogate verdict C: the nothing-to-merge path still runs --verify in the integration tree and reports it; forward-merge-via-epic never reports land-failed for a dependent whose tip is already in <epic>.

Interrogate verdict D: epic close order is land every done task on <epic>, rebase <epic> onto main in the integration tree, full suite and lint on the rebased tip, only then fast-forward main, then the full suite on main; the close summary records main's pre-ff SHA; docs carry this order.
Interrogate verdict E: in landing mode the continue gate emits a MERGE line for every done task not yet in <epic>, and the close refuses while a done task is not in <epic>.

Interrogate verdict F: epics already in progress with legacy <epic>--<task> trees and no <epic> branch upgrade through ticket.py worktrees --integration; cmd_worktrees keeps a live legacy tree's record; plan-execute accepts a recorded legacy tree.

Interrogate verdict G: reviewer and verifier diffs after a task has landed (remediation, audit re-review, forward-merge re-verify) are taken from the task's recorded fork point, not merge-base(HEAD, <epic>).

Interrogate verdict H: the land step instructs the merger to resolve re-conflicts that appear when a rebase drops a dependent's merge-of-<epic> commit, resolving unambiguous ones and otherwise failing land-failed with the conflicting files named.
Interrogate verdict I: slug-collision-guard has an explicit acceptance condition for legacy <epic>--<task> trees and branches still on disk.
